l1: Is Sysprep being run for image capture (/generalize), audit mode testing (/audit), or just OOBE reset (/oobe only)?
What is the exact Sysprep error and where does it point (usually setuperr.log or setupact.log)?
Is this a physical reference machine or a VM template being prepared for cloning?
Has Sysprep been run successfully before on this same base image, or is this the first attempt?
Is this Sysprep run part of an automated build pipeline (e.g. MDT/SCCM task sequence) or a manual one-off capture?
l2: Is an unattend.xml (answer file) being supplied to Sysprep, and if so, which pass is failing (specialize, oobeSystem, etc.)?
Has the machine exceeded the Sysprep rearm limit (default 3 rearms per installation)?
Are any Microsoft Store / provisioned AppX packages installed for a user profile other than the built-in Administrator, which commonly blocks generalize?
Is any non-Microsoft disk encryption, antivirus, or endpoint agent installed that is known to interfere with generalization?

l1: Check C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\Panther\setuperr.log for the specific error and its line context.
Check C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\Panther\setupact.log for the full sequence of actions leading up to the failure.
Confirm the exact Sysprep command-line switches used (/generalize /oobe /shutdown /unattend:<file>).
Run 'slmgr /dlv' to check the current rearm count before attempting another generalize pass.
l2: Search setuperr.log for 'SYSPRP Package ... was installed for a user' — this is the classic per-user AppX package blocker for generalize.
If an unattend.xml is supplied, identify which configuration pass (windowsPE, specialize, oobeSystem, etc.) the failure occurs in from setupact.log.
Check for non-Microsoft agents (AV, DLP, disk encryption) known to hook into the generalize process and either uninstall or use their documented Sysprep-safe removal/reinstall procedure.
If validation fails immediately with a generic error, run Sysprep from an elevated command prompt rather than the GUI tool to capture more verbose console output.

l1: Re-run Sysprep after closing all open applications and ensuring no pending reboot is outstanding.
Confirm the machine has not exceeded its rearm limit; if it has, a fresh installation is required rather than another generalize attempt.
Remove any obviously non-standard user profiles before generalizing.
Retry with a minimal unattend.xml (or none) to isolate whether the answer file itself is the cause.
If Sysprep fails immediately with a generic dialog, check the Windows Event Log (Application) for a Sysprep source event with more detail than the dialog shows.
Confirm the reference machine isn't in the middle of a pending Windows Update install/reboot before running Sysprep.
l2: For 'Package ... was installed for a user' failures, remove the offending per-user provisioned AppX package with 'Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers | Where {$_.PackageFullName -like "*<name>*"} | Remove-AppxPackage' before regeneralizing.

For a specialize-pass failure with a custom unattend.xml, validate the XML against the component schema for that Windows build using the Windows System Image Manager (WSIM/SIM) rather than hand-editing blind.
If a third-party agent is confirmed as the blocker, follow that vendor's documented Sysprep-compatible install/removal sequence (many require uninstall-before-capture, reinstall-after-deploy).
If the rearm limit (3 by default) has been exhausted during repeated testing, rebuild the reference VM/image from a fresh installation rather than continuing to rearm the same instance.

l1: Record the exact Sysprep switches used and whether an unattend.xml was supplied.
Note the current rearm count from 'slmgr /dlv'.
Confirm whether this is a physical reference machine or a VM template.
Note any third-party AV, DLP, or disk-encryption agents installed on the reference machine.
l2: Collect setuperr.log and setupact.log from C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\Panther.
Collect the unattend.xml used, if any.
Collect 'Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers' output to check for per-user provisioned packages that could block generalize.
Collect a list of installed third-party agents/services for cross-reference against known Sysprep-incompatible software.

generalize_fails_appx_package_for_user.title: Sysprep /generalize fails — 'Package ... was installed for a user'

steps.action: Check setuperr.log for the exact line naming the AppX package and the user it was installed for
steps.expect: Confirms the specific per-user provisioned package blocking generalize

steps.action: Run 'Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers' and confirm the named package is present for a non-default user profile
steps.expect: Confirms the package's install scope is the actual blocker

steps.action: Remove the package for that user with 'Remove-AppxPackage' (or remove the offending user profile entirely if it's not needed in the image)
steps.expect: Package no longer shows installed for a non-default user
Sysprep completes successfully and the machine shuts down cleanly for capture

rearm_limit_exhausted.title: Sysprep rearm limit has been exhausted during repeated testing

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /dlv' and check the remaining rearm count
steps.expect: Confirms the rearm count has reached 0

steps.action: Confirm this VM/reference machine has been generalized and rearmed repeatedly during iterative testing
steps.expect: Explains why no rearms remain despite no obvious error in the process itself

steps.action: Rebuild the reference machine or VM template from a fresh installation instead of continuing to reuse the exhausted instance
steps.expect: New instance has a full rearm allowance available

validation_failed_generic_dialog_error.title: Sysprep fails immediately with a generic 'Sysprep was not able to validate...' error

steps.action: Check Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Application for a Sysprep-source event around the failure time
steps.expect: Often surfaces a more specific error than the generic dialog

steps.action: Cross-reference the specific event/error against setuperr.log in the Sysprep Panther folder
steps.expect: Confirms the specific blocking condition (e.g. pending update, per-user AppX package, third-party agent)

steps.action: Resolve the specific blocking condition identified (complete any pending update/reboot first, then address AppX/agent issues as needed)

audit_mode_stuck_after_ctrl_shift_f3.title: Machine hangs or loops when entering/exiting Audit mode

steps.action: Confirm whether the hang occurs entering Audit mode (Ctrl+Shift+F3 at OOBE) or exiting it back to OOBE/generalize
steps.expect: Narrows down which transition is actually failing

steps.action: Check setupact.log for the last logged action before the hang, and confirm no application installed during audit mode is holding a UI dialog open in the background
steps.expect: Identifies a specific blocking app/dialog or a genuine setup engine hang

steps.action: Close any blocking application dialogs, or if the engine itself is hung, restart and retry the transition; remove any recently-installed app suspected of interfering
Repeat the audit mode entry/exit cycle once more to confirm stability
steps.expect: No repeat hang on the same transition
